findings.summary: Provider runtime always resumes invented IDs, so a new Claude or Codex conversation cannot be created.
findings.requiredClosure: Model create versus resume explicitly; Claude uses pinned creation then resume, Codex uses thread/start then returned ID for resume, and fakes reject nonexistent resume.

findings.summary: Subscription authentication diagnostics accept any zero exit and are not wired through IPC or the real first-run flow.

findings.summary: Filesystem mutations precede durable migration journal transitions and rollback can delete the last usable migrated copy.
findings.requiredClosure: Use write-ahead intent stages and presence reconciliation, restore and verify prior copy before removing new target, and inject crashes before and after every rename, delete, and journal write for replay and rollback.

findings.summary: Context and evidence delivery state advances before provider success and Resume reconstructs the cursor incorrectly.

findings.summary: The provider boundary buffers until child close, preventing progressive sections and preserving no partial output on cancellation.

findings.summary: Session commands, provider turns, and snapshot writes are not serialized, and Reset cannot cancel compact turns.

findings.requiredClosure: Restore composition-root capture, queue, reset, movement, and shortcut behavior through typed session commands; remove legacy helper view authority and add production regression coverage.
